name: BPC-157
summary: BPC-157 is a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide studied mainly in animal models for tissue repair and inflammation. FDA identified five small human clinical studies in its 2026 review, but the evidence is short-duration, heterogeneous, and insufficient to establish clinical efficacy or long-term safety; BPC-157 is not FDA-approved.
description: BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound-157) is a synthetic peptide derived from a partial sequence found in human gastric juice and widely discussed for tendon, ligament, gut-lining, and recovery claims. Preclinical rodent and in vitro studies dominate the evidence base. FDA's 2026 review identified five human clinical studies, including two older rectal-enema studies and three very small modern reports; these data document human exposure but do not establish replicated clinical efficacy, an approved dosing strategy, or long-term safety. BPC-157 is not FDA-approved as a finished drug product.
bioavailability: Reported via subcutaneous injection or oral capsule in RUO products; oral bioavailability of the intact peptide is not well characterized in humans.
safetyNotes: No large-scale human safety data exists. RUO-sourced product purity and sterility are not independently verified. Physician oversight is strongly recommended rather than self-directed use.
dosage: No established consumer dosing protocol; see full guide article for regulatory and safety context.
typical_dosage: No established consumer dosing protocol; see full guide article for regulatory and safety context.
contraindications: Active cancer or cancer history (theoretical angiogenesis/tumor-growth concern)
unsupervised RUO product use without physician oversight
No established pharmacokinetic drug-interaction data exists
theoretical caution combining with other growth-promoting or angiogenic peptides.
regulatory_changelog: 2023-04/2026: FDA Category 2 restricted (503A bulk substances). 2026-04-22: Removed from Category 2 after nomination withdrawals; this did not place BPC-157 on the 503A Bulks List. 2026-07-23: FDA PCAC voted to recommend BPC-157-related bulk drug substances for the 503A Bulks List. The advisory recommendation is non-binding and did not itself create a final 503A rule; as of 2026-08-26, no final FDA rule adding BPC-157 was located.
